_comment: Weights must sum to 1.0. Hygiene and attribution carry the most because they are what makes hours usable for client billing: hygiene says the hours are remembered rather than reconstructed, attribution says we know whose budget they came out of. This file holds rules and thresholds only. Real people live in roster.json, which is gitignored.

hygiene._comment: A workday counts only if it holds an entry that was created within grace_days of the day it covers. Set grace_days to 1 so logging yesterday this morning still counts, but reconstructing a fortnight on Friday night does not.

coverage._comment: Over-logging counts against you as much as under-logging. tolerance_ratio is the band inside which coverage scores a clean 1.0.

attribution._comment: Leave attributable_project_gids empty for the first baseline period. While it is empty, any entry with a non-null attributable_to counts and the score is flagged loose, because it cannot tell a client project from a catch-all task. Fill the allowlist once you know which projects are genuinely billable.

nudge._comment: Slack DM only, daily, to the person and nobody else at every level. Nothing here copies a manager. email_enabled is off because the team lives in Slack; turn it on only for someone who genuinely does not read Slack. max_per_week is a hard stop: by the fifth day in one week the daily nudge has demonstrably not worked on that person, and a fifth identical message only teaches them to filter it. That case belongs to the weekly draft in playbooks/friday-review.md, which a human sends. behind_ratio is the share of expected hours a person must have logged week-to-date to be left alone.

persistence._comment: Defines 'constantly not following the process' for the weekly draft. Someone is flagged when either condition holds across the lookback: their weekly score fell below the gate's individual_floor in at least weeks_below_floor_to_flag of those weeks, or they ran a nudge streak of nudge_streak_to_flag or more weekdays in any single week. One bad week is a bad week; two out of three is a pattern.

submission._comment: The week closes Friday at cutoff_local_hour in each person's own timezone, so Manila closes before Johannesburg, which closes before Central European Time. cutoff_weekday is 0 for Monday, so 4 is Friday.

approval_endpoint._comment: Asana's timesheet approval status API is recent, so verify the exact collection path against this workspace before trusting the on-time score. Leave path empty until verified. While it is empty, on_time_submission is reported as unavailable and the other three weights are renormalized, with the output flagged partial. Never guess a path here.

_program_start: The first day that counts. Time logged before it stays in Asana and is real work, it is simply not scored and never triggers a nudge, because judging people against a rule before they were told about it produces an argument rather than a habit. It also keeps one bad pre-launch week out of the two-period gate. Set it once, then leave it alone.
_holidays: Days nobody is expected to log. They drop out of expected hours, so a four-day week is scored as a four-day week rather than as everyone being twenty percent behind.
